sanskrit: tasmin pratihate 'stre tu rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ krodhaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ cakre krodhāc cāstram anantaram
english: When that weapon was repelled, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, doubled his fury, and from that fury he immediately discharged another missile.

sanskrit: mayena vihitaṃ raudram anyad astraṃ mahādyutiḥ utsraṣṭuṃ rāvaṇo ghoraṃ rāghavāya pracakrame
english: That great-resplendent one, Rāvaṇa, made ready to release against Rāghava another terrible weapon fashioned by Maya, dreadful in its power.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūlāni niścerur gadāś ca musalāni ca kārmukād dīpyamānāni vajrasārāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: Then from his bow there flew out tridents, maces, and pestles blazing with fire, all hard as the thunderbolt, on every side.

sanskrit: kūṭamudgarapāśāś ca dīptāś cāśanayas tathā niṣpetur vividhās tīkṣṇā vātā iva yugakṣaye
english: Hammers with knobbed heads, nooses, and burning thunderbolts also streamed forth, sharp and varied, like the winds at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ rāghavaḥ śrīmān uttamāstravidāṃ varaḥ jaghāna paramāstreṇa gandharveṇa mahādyutiḥ
english: That illustrious Rāghava, the foremost among the greatest knowers of weaponry, of immense splendour, countered that weapon with the supreme Gāndharva missile.

sanskrit: tasmin pratihate 'stre tu rāghaveṇa mahātmanā rāvaṇaḥ krodhatāmrākṣaḥ sauram astram udīrayat
english: When that weapon was neutralised by the great-souled Rāghava, Rāvaṇa, his eyes reddened with rage, discharged the Solar missile.

sanskrit: tataś cakrāṇi niṣpetur bhāsvarāṇi mahānti ca kārmukād bhīmavegasya daśagrīvasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then blazing discs, vast and brilliant, flew out from the bow of the ten-necked one, that intelligent being of terrible velocity.

sanskrit: tair āsīd gaganaṃ dīptaṃ saṃpatadbhir itas tataḥ patadbhiś ca diśo dīptaiś candrasūryagrahair iva
english: With those discs flashing hither and thither and falling in all directions, the sky was ablaze, as if with the fiery orbs of the moon, the sun, and the planets.

sanskrit: tāni ciccheda bāṇaughaiś cakrāṇi tu sa rāghavaḥ āyudhāni vicitrāṇi rāvaṇasya camūmukhe
english: Rāghava shattered all those discs and the varied weapons of Rāvaṇa in the forefront of battle with floods of arrows.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ tu hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ vivyādha daśabhir bāṇair rāmaṃ sarveṣu marmasu
english: Seeing that weapon destroyed, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, pierced Rāma in all his vital spots with ten arrows.

sanskrit: sa viddho daśabhir bāṇair mahākārmukaniḥsṛtaiḥ rāvaṇena mahātejā na prākampata rāghavaḥ
english: Though pierced by those ten arrows shot from the great bow of Rāvaṇa, the greatly lustrous Rāghava did not tremble.

sanskrit: tato vivyādha gātreṣu sarveṣu samitiṃjayaḥ rāghavas tu susaṃkruddho rāvaṇaṃ bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Rāghava, triumphant in battle, filled with great wrath, pierced Rāvaṇa in all his limbs with many arrows.

sanskrit: etasminn antare kruddho rāghavasyānujo balī lakṣmaṇaḥ sāyakān sapta jagrāha paravīrahā
english: Meanwhile, the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava's younger brother, who was enraged and a slayer of enemy heroes, took up seven arrows.

sanskrit: taiḥ sāyakair mahāvegai rāvaṇasya mahādyutiḥ dhvajaṃ manuṣyaśīrṣaṃ tu tasya ciccheda naikadhā
english: With those arrows of great velocity, the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa, of immense splendour, split Rāvaṇa's banner bearing human skulls into many pieces.

sanskrit: sāratheś cāpi bāṇena śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam jahāra lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān nairṛtasya mahābalaḥ
english: And with another arrow the illustrious and greatly powerful Lakṣmaṇa struck off the head of the charioteer of the lord of the rākṣasas—that head adorned with gleaming earrings.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇaiś ca ciccheda dhanur gajakaropamam lakṣmaṇo rākṣasendrasya pañcabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa also shattered the bow of the lord of the rākṣasas—that bow resembling the rut-post of an elephant—with five sharp arrows.

sanskrit: nīlameghanibhāṃś cāsya sadaśvān parvatopamān jaghānāplutya gadayā rāvaṇasya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And Vibhīṣaṇa, leaping forward, slew with his mace the excellent horses of Rāvaṇa—those horses dark as rain-clouds and huge as mountains.

sanskrit: hatāśvād vegavān vegād avaplutya mahārathāt krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ bhrātaraṃ prati rāvaṇaḥ
english: With his horses slain, Rāvaṇa swiftly leaped down from the great chariot and directed his fierce rage toward his own brother.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahāśaktir dīptāṃ dīptāśanīm iva vibhīṣaṇāya cikṣepa rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
english: Then the powerful lord of rākṣasas, of great might, hurled a blazing śakti lance at Vibhīṣaṇa—a lance blazing like a flaming thunderbolt.

sanskrit: aprāptām eva tāṃ bāṇais tribhiś ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ athodatiṣṭhat saṃnādo vānarāṇāṃ tadā raṇe
english: Before it even reached him, Lakṣmaṇa cut it down with three arrows. Then a great shout arose from the monkeys in the battle.

sanskrit: sā papāta tridhā chinnā śaktiḥ kāñcanamālinī savisphuliṅgā jvalitā maholkeva divaś cyutā
english: That śakti lance, garlanded with gold and cut in three pieces, fell sparkling and blazing like a great meteor fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃbhāvitatarāṃ kālenāpi durāsadām jagrāha vipulāṃ śaktiṃ dīpyamānāṃ svatejasā
english: Then he seized another great śakti, still more formidable, hard to withstand even by Time itself, blazing with its own inherent radiance.

sanskrit: sā veginā balavatā rāvaṇena durātmanā jajvāla sumahāghorā śakrāśanisamaprabhā
english: In the swift and powerful hands of the wicked Rāvaṇa it blazed with supremely dreadful fire, its brilliance equal to Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīro lakṣmaṇas taṃ vibhīṣaṇam prāṇasaṃśayam āpannaṃ tūrṇam evābhyapadyata
english: In that very instant the heroic Lakṣmaṇa swiftly went to Vibhīṣaṇa, who had fallen into danger of losing his life.

sanskrit: taṃ vimokṣayituṃ vīraś cāpam āyamya lakṣmaṇaḥ rāvaṇaṃ śaktihastaṃ taṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: To free him, the heroic Lakṣmaṇa drew his bow and covered Rāvaṇa, who held the śakti in hand, with a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: kīryamāṇaḥ śaraugheṇa visṛṣṭena mahātmanā na prahartuṃ manaś cakre vimukhīkṛtavikramaḥ
english: Overwhelmed by the flood of arrows released by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, his valour checked and turned aside, Rāvaṇa's mind could not fix itself on striking a blow.

sanskrit: mokṣitaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇena sa rāvaṇaḥ lakṣmaṇābhimukhas tiṣṭhann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing his brother freed by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāvaṇa turned to face Lakṣmaṇa and spoke these words.

sanskrit: mokṣitas te balaślāghin yasmād evaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ vimucya rākṣasaṃ śaktis tvayīyaṃ vinipātyate
english: "You who boast of your strength—since you have freed Vibhīṣaṇa the rākṣasa in this way, this śakti of mine shall now be aimed at you instead.

sanskrit: eṣā te hṛdayaṃ bhittvā śaktir lohitalakṣaṇā madbāhuparighotsṛṣṭā prāṇān ādāya yāsyati
english: This śakti, red with its iron marks, hurled from my arm-like iron bar, shall pierce your heart and carry away your life."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā tāṃ śaktim aṣṭaghaṇṭāṃ mahāsvanām mayena māyāvihitām amoghāṃ śatrughātinīm
english: Having spoken thus, he took up that śakti fitted with eight great bells and loud-sounding, fashioned by Maya's magic, never failing, a slayer of enemies—

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇāya samuddiśya jvalantīm iva tejasā rāvaṇaḥ paramakruddhaś cikṣepa ca nanāda ca
english: —aiming it at Lakṣmaṇa, blazing as it were with its own energy. Rāvaṇa, supremely wrathful, hurled it and roared aloud.

sanskrit: sā kṣiptā bhīmavegena śakrāśanisamasvanā śaktir abhyapatad vegāl lakṣmaṇaṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Hurled with terrible velocity, sounding like Indra's thunderbolt, that śakti flew swiftly at Lakṣmaṇa in the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: tām anuvyāharac chaktim āpatantīṃ sa rāghavaḥ svastyas tu lakṣmaṇāyeti moghā bhava hatodyamā
english: Rāghava cried after that oncoming śakti: "May Lakṣmaṇa be safe! Be futile—your assault is destroyed!"

sanskrit: nyapatat sā mahāvegā lakṣmaṇasya mahorasi jihvevoragarājasya dīpyamānā mahādyutiḥ
english: That śakti of great velocity fell blazing with immense radiance upon the broad chest of Lakṣmaṇa, like the tongue of the king of serpents.

sanskrit: tato rāvaṇavegena sudūram avagāḍhayā śaktyā nirbhinnahṛdayaḥ papāta bhuvi lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, his heart pierced through by the śakti driven deep by Rāvaṇa's force, fell upon the earth.

sanskrit: tadavasthaṃ samīpastho lakṣmaṇaṃ prekṣya rāghavaḥ bhrātṛsnehān mahātejā viṣaṇṇahṛdayo 'bhavat
english: Standing close by and seeing Lakṣmaṇa in that condition, the greatly resplendent Rāghava, out of his love for his brother, became heavy of heart.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam anudhyāya bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ babhūva saṃrabdhataro yugānta iva pāvakaḥ
english: He brooded for a moment, his eyes blurred with tears, then blazed forth with greater ferocity, like the fire at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: na viṣādasya kālo 'yam iti saṃcintya rāghavaḥ cakre sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhe dhṛtaḥ
english: Reflecting that "this is not the time for despair," Rāghava resolved on the slaying of Rāvaṇa and waged battle with tremendous uproar.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tato rāmaḥ śaktyā bhinnaṃ mahāhave lakṣmaṇaṃ rudhirādigdhaṃ sapannagam ivācalam
english: Rāma then saw Lakṣmaṇa in the great battle, pierced by the śakti, smeared with blood, lying like a mountain with its serpents.

sanskrit: tām api prahitāṃ śaktiṃ rāvaṇena balīyasā yatnatas te hariśreṣṭhā na śekur avamarditum arditāś caiva bāṇaughaiḥ kṣiprahastena rakṣasā
english: Even those foremost monkeys could not destroy that śakti hurled by the mighty Rāvaṇa, try as they might—they were themselves tormented by floods of arrows from the swift-handed rākṣasa.

sanskrit: saumitriṃ sā vinirbhidya praviṣṭā dharaṇītalam tāṃ karābhyāṃ parāmṛśya rāmaḥ śaktiṃ bhayāvahām babhañja samare kruddho balavad vicakarṣa ca
english: After piercing Saumitri it had entered the earth. Rāma, enraged in battle, seized that dreadful śakti with both hands and forcefully broke and extracted it.

sanskrit: tasya niṣkarṣataḥ śaktiṃ rāvaṇena balīyasā śarāḥ sarveṣu gātreṣu pātitā marmabhedinaḥ
english: Even as he drew it out, the mighty Rāvaṇa rained down arrows that pierced him in all his limbs, cutting through his vital points.

sanskrit: acintayitvā tān bāṇān samāśliṣya ca lakṣmaṇam abravīc ca hanūmantaṃ sugrīvaṃ caiva rāghavaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ parivāryeha tiṣṭhadhvaṃ vānarottamāḥ
english: Paying no heed to those arrows, Rāghava embraced Lakṣmaṇa and then spoke to Hanūmat and Sugrīva: "Surround and guard Lakṣmaṇa here, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: parākramasya kālo 'yaṃ saṃprāpto me cirepsitaḥ pāpātmāyaṃ daśagrīvo vadhyatāṃ pāpaniścayaḥ kāṅkṣitaḥ stokakasyeva gharmānte meghadarśanam
english: "The moment for valour has arrived—long desired by me. This wicked-souled ten-necked one, resolute in evil, shall be slain. I have longed for this as the chataka bird longs to see the cloud at summer's end."

sanskrit: asmin muhūrte nacirāt satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi vaḥ arāvaṇam arāmaṃ vā jagad drakṣyatha vānarāḥ
english: "In this very moment, very soon, I swear truly to you: you monkeys shall see a world either without Rāvaṇa or without Rāma."

sanskrit: rājyanāśaṃ vane vāsaṃ daṇḍake paridhāvanam vaidehyāś ca parāmarśaṃ rakṣobhiś ca samāgamam
english: "The loss of the kingdom, the sojourn in the forest, the wandering through Daṇḍaka, the seizure of Vaidehī, and the encounter with the rākṣasas—

sanskrit: prāptaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahad ghoraṃ kleśaṃ ca nirayopamam adya sarvam ahaṃ tyakṣye hatvā taṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
english: "—all that great and dreadful suffering, all that affliction resembling hell—I shall today put an end to all of it by slaying Rāvaṇa in battle."

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ vānaraṃ sainyaṃ samānītam idaṃ mayā sugrīvaś ca kṛto rājye nihatvā vālinaṃ raṇe
english: "For this very purpose I assembled this monkey army, and for this I made Sugrīva king by slaying Vālin in battle."

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ sāgaraḥ krāntaḥ setur baddhaś ca sāgare so 'yam adya raṇe pāpaś cakṣurviṣayam āgataḥ
english: "For this very purpose the ocean was crossed and the bridge built over the sea. That wicked one has now come within the range of my sight in battle."

sanskrit: cakṣurviṣayam āgamya nāyaṃ jīvitum arhati dṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭiviṣasyeva sarpasya mama rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Having come within range of my gaze, Rāvaṇa does not deserve to live—as no creature can survive the gaze of a serpent whose very sight is venom."

sanskrit: svasthāḥ paśyata durdharṣā yuddhaṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ āsīnāḥ parvatāgreṣu mamedaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
english: "Be at ease, O invincible chiefs of monkeys, and watch from the mountain-tops this battle between me and Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: adya rāmasya rāmatvaṃ paśyantu mama saṃyuge trayo lokāḥ sagandharvāḥ sadevāḥ sarṣicāraṇāḥ
english: "Today let the three worlds, together with gandharvas, gods, sages, and cāraṇas, behold the Rāma-ness of Rāma in my combat."

sanskrit: adya karma kariṣyāmi yal lokāḥ sacarācarāḥ sadevāḥ kathayiṣyanti yāvad bhūmir dhariṣyati
english: "Today I shall perform a deed that all the worlds, with all their moving and unmoving creatures, together with the gods, shall speak of as long as the earth endures."

sanskrit: evam uktvā śitair bāṇais taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ ājaghāna daśagrīvaṃ raṇe rāmaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Rāma, composed and focused, struck the ten-necked one in battle with sharp arrows adorned with heated gold.

sanskrit: atha pradīptair nārācair musalaiś cāpi rāvaṇaḥ abhyavarṣat tadā rāmaṃ dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa poured down upon Rāma blazing iron arrows and maces like a rain-cloud pouring streams.

sanskrit: rāmarāvaṇamuktānām anyonyam abhinighnatām śarāṇāṃ ca śarāṇāṃ ca babhūva tumulaḥ svanaḥ
english: The noise of the arrows of Rāma and Rāvaṇa, flying from both sides and striking each other, was tremendous.

sanskrit: te bhinnāś ca vikīrṇāś ca rāmarāvaṇayoḥ śarāḥ antarikṣāt pradīptāgrā nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Those arrows of Rāma and Rāvaṇa, broken and scattered, with their tips aflame, fell from the sky to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tayor jyātalanirghoṣo rāmarāvaṇayor mahān trāsanaḥ sarvabūtānāṃ sa babhūvādbhutopamaḥ
english: The great twanging sound of the bowstrings of those two—Rāma and Rāvaṇa—which struck terror into all beings, was beyond compare in its wonder.

sanskrit: sa kīryamāṇaḥ śarajālavṛṣṭibhir mahātmanā dīptadhanuṣmatārditaḥ bhayāt pradudrāva sametya rāvaṇo yathānilenābhihato balāhakaḥ
english: Pelted with torrents of arrow-nets by the great-souled one, tormented by him who held a blazing bow, Rāvaṇa fled out of fear, even as he had come, like a rain-cloud struck and driven off by the wind.

sanskrit: sa dattvā tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ visṛjann eva bāṇaughān suṣeṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Having given fierce battle to the wicked-souled Rāvaṇa and still releasing floods of arrows, he spoke these words to Suṣeṇa.

sanskrit: eṣa rāvaṇavegena lakṣmaṇaḥ patitaḥ kṣitau sarpavad veṣṭate vīro mama śokam udīrayan
english: "Lakṣmaṇa has fallen to the ground by the force of Rāvaṇa's blow; the hero writhes like a serpent, rousing anguish in me."

sanskrit: śoṇitārdram imaṃ vīraṃ prāṇair iṣṭataraṃ mama paśyato mama kā śaktir yoddhuṃ paryākulātmanaḥ
english: "Seeing this hero drenched in blood—he who is dearer to me than life—what power have I to fight, when my spirit is so distraught?"

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa samaraślāghī bhrātā me śubhalakṣaṇaḥ yadi pañcatvam āpannaḥ prāṇair me kiṃ sukhena vā
english: "This is my brother who gloried in battle, marked with auspicious signs. If he has attained the five elements, what use to me are my own life or happiness?"

sanskrit: lajjatīva hi me vīryaṃ bhraśyatīva karād dhanuḥ sāyakā vyavasīdanti dṛṣṭir bāṣpavaśaṃ gatā cintā me vardhate tīvrā mumūrṣā copajāyate
english: "My heroic energy seems to shrink with shame, my bow seems to slip from my hand, my arrows falter, my sight is overcome with tears; my anguish intensifies sharply, and the desire to die arises in me."

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena durātmanā paraṃ viṣādam āpanno vilalāpākulendriyaḥ
english: Seeing his brother struck down by the wicked-souled Rāvaṇa, he fell into deep despair and lamented with senses overwhelmed.

sanskrit: na hi yuddhena me kāryaṃ naiva prāṇair na sītayā bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ raṇapāṃsuṣu
english: "Neither battle nor life nor even Sītā concerns me, having seen my brother Lakṣmaṇa struck down in the dust of combat."

sanskrit: kiṃ me rājyena kiṃ prāṇair yuddhe kāryaṃ na vidyate yatrāyaṃ nihataḥ śete raṇamūrdhani lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "What use to me is a kingdom? What use my life? I have no purpose in battle while Lakṣmaṇa lies struck down in the forefront of the fight."

sanskrit: rāmam āśvāsayan vīraḥ suṣeṇo vākyam abravīt na mṛto 'yaṃ mahābāhur lakṣmaṇo lakṣmivardhanaḥ
english: The heroic Suṣeṇa, comforting Rāma, spoke these words: "This great-armed Lakṣmaṇa, increaser of glory, is not dead."

sanskrit: na cāsya vikṛtaṃ vaktraṃ nāpi śyāmaṃ na niṣprabham suprabhaṃ ca prasannaṃ ca mukham asyābhilakṣyate
english: "His face is not distorted, nor dark, nor without radiance. His face can be seen to be bright and serene."

sanskrit: padmaraktatalau hastau suprasanne ca locane evaṃ na vidyate rūpaṃ gatāsūnāṃ viśāṃ pate māṃ viṣādaṃ kṛthā vīra saprāṇo 'yam ariṃdama
english: "His palms are red as lotus flowers, and his eyes are calm and clear. Such appearance does not belong to the dead, O lord of men. Do not despair, O hero; he lives yet, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: ākhyāsyate prasuptasya srastagātrasya bhūtale socchvāsaṃ hṛdayaṃ vīra kampamānaṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: "Of one who lies as if asleep on the ground with relaxed limbs, his heart heaving with breath, trembling again and again—this tells us he is alive."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vākyajñaḥ suṣeṇo rāghavaṃ vacaḥ samīpastham uvācedaṃ hanūmantam abhitvaran
english: Having spoken those words to Rāghava, Suṣeṇa, skilled in speech, spoke these further words in haste to Hanūmat who stood near.

sanskrit: saumya śīghram ito gatvā śailam oṣadhiparvatam pūrvaṃ hi kathito yo 'sau vīra jāmbavatā śubhaḥ
english: "O gentle one, go swiftly from here to the Oṣadhi mountain—the auspicious peak that was described before by the heroic Jāmbavat."

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe śikhare tasya jātām oṣadhim ānaya viśalyakaraṇī nāma viśalyakaraṇīṃ śubhām
english: "On the southern peak of that mountain grows an herb; bring it here—the Viśalyakaraṇī, the auspicious herb known as Viśalyakaraṇī."

sanskrit: sauvarṇakaraṇīṃ cāpi tathā saṃjīvanīm api saṃdhānakaraṇīṃ cāpi gatvā śīghram ihānaya saṃjīvanārthaṃ vīrasya lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Bring also the Sauvarṇakaraṇī and the Saṃjīvanī, and the Saṃdhānakaraṇī—go quickly and bring them here for the restoration of the heroic and great-souled Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: ity evam ukto hanumān gatvā cauṣadhiparvatam cintām abhyagamac chrīmān ajānaṃs tā mahauṣadhīḥ
english: Thus instructed, Hanūmat, the illustrious one, went to the Oṣadhi mountain and fell into bewilderment, not recognising those great medicinal herbs.

sanskrit: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā māruter amitaujasaḥ idam eva gamiṣyāmi gṛhītvā śikharaṃ gireḥ
english: Then a thought arose in the mind of that son of the Wind of immeasurable might: "I shall take the very peak of the mountain and carry it there."

sanskrit: agṛhya yadi gacchāmi viśalyakaraṇīm aham kālātyayena doṣaḥ syād vaiklavyaṃ ca mahad bhavet
english: "If I go without taking the Viśalyakaraṇī, time will have passed beyond saving, and great confusion will result."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya hanumān gatvā kṣipraṃ mahābalaḥ utpapāta gṛhītvā tu hanūmāñ śikharaṃ gireḥ
english: Having thus deliberated, the mighty Hanūmat went quickly and, seizing the peak of the mountain, leaped up into the air with it.

sanskrit: oṣadhīr nāvagachāmi tā ahaṃ haripuṃgava tad idaṃ śikharaṃ kṛtsnaṃ gires tasyāhṛtaṃ mayā
english: "I could not identify those herbs, O foremost of monkeys, so I have brought the whole peak of that mountain."

sanskrit: evaṃ kathayamānaṃ taṃ praśasya pavanātmajam suṣeṇo vānaraśreṣṭho jagrāhotpāṭya cauṣadhīḥ
english: Praising the wind-god's son who spoke thus, Suṣeṇa, best of monkeys, plucked and took the herbs from it.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃkṣodayitvā tām oṣadhiṃ vānarottamaḥ lakṣmaṇasya dadau nastaḥ suṣeṇaḥ sumahādyutiḥ
english: Then Suṣeṇa, best of monkeys and of great splendour, crushed that herb and held it to Lakṣmaṇa's nostrils to inhale.

sanskrit: saśalyaḥ sa samāghrāya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā viśalyo virujaḥ śīghram udatiṣṭhan mahītalāt
english: Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy heroes, had breathed in the herb even while the lance was still in him; then, the lance freed and pain gone, he swiftly rose up from the earth.

sanskrit: samutthitaṃ te harayo bhūtalāt prekṣya lakṣmaṇam sādhu sādhv iti suprītāḥ suṣeṇaṃ pratyapūjayan
english: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa rise up from the ground, the monkeys, greatly delighted, cried "Well done! Well done!" and honoured Suṣeṇa.

sanskrit: ehy ehīty abravīd rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ paravīrahā sasvaje snehagāḍhaṃ ca bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
english: Rāma said "Come, come" to Lakṣmaṇa, that slayer of enemy heroes, and embraced him with deep affection, his eyes brimming with tears.

sanskrit: abravīc ca pariṣvajya saumitriṃ rāghavas tadā diṣṭyā tvāṃ vīra paśyāmi maraṇāt punar āgatam
english: Embracing Saumitri, Rāghava said: "By good fortune I see you, O hero, returned from death."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitenārthaḥ sītayā ca jayena vā ko hi me jīvitenārthas tvayi pañcatvam āgate
english: "My life would have no purpose, nor would Sītā, nor victory—what purpose could my life have had if you had been dissolved into the five elements?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadatas tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ khinnaḥ śithilayā vācā lakṣmaṇo vākyam abravīt
english: As the great-souled Rāghava was speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa, distressed and with halting speech, answered him with these words.

sanskrit: tāṃ pratijñāṃ pratijñāya purā satyaparākrama laghuḥ kaś cid ivāsattvo naivaṃ vaktum ihārhasi
english: "You who are resolute in truth and made that vow in days past—you should not speak so here, like some slight and unworthy man."

sanskrit: na pratijñāṃ hi kurvanti vitathāṃ sādhavo 'nagha lakṣaṇaṃ hi mahat tv asya pratijñāparipālanam
english: "The good do not make vows in vain, O sinless one; the keeping of a vow is the great mark of such a man."

sanskrit: nairāśyam upagantuṃ te tad alaṃ matkṛte 'nagha vadhena rāvaṇasyādya pratijñām anupālaya
english: "It is not proper for you to fall into despair on my account, O sinless one. Today, uphold your vow by slaying Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: na jīvan yāsyate śatrus tava bāṇapathaṃ gataḥ nardatas tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrasya siṃhasyeva mahāgajaḥ
english: "No enemy who enters the path of your arrows shall depart alive—no more than a great elephant can depart alive from a roaring lion with sharp fangs."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu vadham icchāmi śīghram asya durātmanaḥ yāvad astaṃ na yāty eṣa kṛtakarmā divākaraḥ
english: "And I desire the swift slaying of that wicked-souled one—before the sun, whose deeds are done, descends to set."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena tu tad vākyam uktaṃ śrutvā sa rāghavaḥ rāvaṇāya śarān ghorān visasarja camūmukhe
english: Hearing those words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava released terrible arrows at Rāvaṇa in the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: daśagrīvo rathasthas tu rāmaṃ vajropamaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghāna mahāghorair dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: The ten-necked one, standing in his chariot, struck Rāma with exceedingly dreadful arrows resembling thunderbolts, like a rain-cloud with its streams.

sanskrit: dīptapāvakasaṃkāśaiḥ śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ nirbibheda raṇe rāmo daśagrīvaṃ samāhitaḥ
english: Rāma, composed and focused, pierced the ten-necked one in battle with arrows blazing like fire and adorned with gold.

sanskrit: bhūmisthitasya rāmasya rathasthasya ca rakṣasaḥ na samaṃ yuddham ity āhur devagandharvadānavāḥ
english: "The battle is not equal—Rāma standing on the ground and the rākṣasa standing in a chariot," so said the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgaḥ kiṃkiṇīśatabhūṣitaḥ taruṇādityasaṃkāśo vaidūryamayakūbaraḥ
english: Then a chariot with limbs ornamented with gold, adorned with hundreds of small bells, resembling the newly risen sun, with a yoke-pole made of vaidūrya gems—

sanskrit: sadaśvaiḥ kāñcanāpīḍair yuktaḥ śvetaprakīrṇakaiḥ haribhiḥ sūryasaṃkāśair hemajālavibhūṣitaiḥ
english: —yoked with excellent horses wearing golden headpieces, with white scattered manes, tawny horses bright as the sun, adorned with a net of gold—

sanskrit: rukmaveṇudhvajaḥ śrīmān devarājaratho varaḥ abhyavartata kākutstham avatīrya triviṣṭapāt
english: —bearing a banner-staff of gold, the auspicious and supreme chariot of the king of the gods, descended from the heavens and drove up to Kākutstha.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmaṃ sapratodo rathe sthitaḥ prāñjalir mātalir vākyaṃ sahasrākṣasya sārathiḥ
english: And Mātali, the charioteer of the thousand-eyed Indra, standing in the chariot with his goad, addressed Rāma with joined palms and spoke these words.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣeṇa kākutstha ratho 'yaṃ vijayāya te dattas tava mahāsattva śrīmāñ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: "This chariot, O Kākutstha, has been given by the thousand-eyed Indra for your victory—this auspicious chariot that destroys enemies, O great being."

sanskrit: idam aindraṃ mahaccāpaṃ kavacaṃ cāgnisaṃnibham śarāś cādityasaṃkāśāḥ śaktiś ca vimalā śitāḥ
english: "Here is the great Aindra bow, and armour resembling fire, and arrows bright as the sun, and a śakti lance, pure and keen."

sanskrit: āruhyemaṃ rathaṃ vīra rākṣasaṃ jahi rāvaṇam mayā sārathinā rāma mahendra iva dānavān
english: "Mount this chariot, O hero, and slay the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, with me as your charioteer, O Rāma—even as great Indra slew the dānavas."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa parikramya rathaṃ tam abhivādya ca āruroha tadā rāmo lokāṃl lakṣmyā virājayan
english: Thus addressed, Rāma circumambulated the chariot, saluted it reverently, and mounted it—illuminating the worlds with his splendour.

sanskrit: tad babhūvādbhutaṃ yuddhaṃ dvairathaṃ lomaharṣaṇam rāmasya ca mahābāho rāvaṇasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: Then there was a wondrous battle between two chariots, hair-raising, between the great-armed Rāma and the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: sa gāndharveṇa gāndharvaṃ daivaṃ daivena rāghavaḥ astraṃ rākṣasarājasya jaghāna paramāstravit
english: That Rāghava, supreme knower of missiles, countered the Gāndharva weapon with the Gāndharva, and the divine weapon of the rākṣasa king with the divine.

sanskrit: astraṃ tu paramaṃ ghoraṃ rākṣasaṃ rākasādhipaḥ sasarja paramakruddhaḥ punar eva niśācaraḥ
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas, that night-wanderer, supremely enraged, released once more a most terrible and dreadful rākṣasa weapon.

sanskrit: te rāvaṇadhanurmuktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ abhyavartanta kākutsthaṃ sarpā bhūtvā mahāviṣāḥ
english: Those golden-adorned arrows released from Rāvaṇa's bow advanced upon Kākutstha having transformed into great venomous serpents.

sanskrit: te dīptavadanā dīptaṃ vamanto jvalanaṃ mukhaiḥ rāmam evābhyavartanta vyāditāsyā bhayānakāḥ
english: With blazing mouths vomiting fire and flame, they advanced upon Rāma alone, with gaping jaws, terrifying.

sanskrit: tair vāsukisamasparśair dīptabhogair mahāviṣaiḥ diśaś ca saṃtatāḥ sarvāḥ pradiśaś ca samāvṛtāḥ
english: With those blazing-bodied, greatly venomous ones whose touch was like Vāsuki's, all the directions and the intermediate directions were covered and filled.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā pannagān rāmaḥ samāpatata āhave astraṃ gārutmataṃ ghoraṃ prāduścakre bhayāvaham
english: Seeing those serpents rushing toward him in battle, Rāma manifested the dreadful and fear-inspiring Gārutmat missile.

sanskrit: te rāghavadhanurmuktā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śikhiprabhāḥ suparṇāḥ kāñcanā bhūtvā viceruḥ sarpaśatravaḥ
english: Those arrows released from Rāghava's bow, with golden nocks and flame-bright tips, became golden suparṇas—enemies of serpents—and flew forth.

sanskrit: te tān sarvāñ śarāñ jaghnuḥ sarparūpān mahājavān suparṇarūpā rāmasya viśikhāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Those shape-shifting arrows of Rāma, now in the form of suparṇas, slew all those swift-moving arrows that had taken the form of serpents.

sanskrit: astre pratihate kruddho rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ abhyavarṣat tadā rāmaṃ ghorābhiḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: His weapon neutralised, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, enraged, then showered Rāma with dreadful torrents of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa rāmam akliṣṭakāriṇam ardayitvā śaraugheṇa mātaliṃ pratyavidhyata
english: Having tormented Rāma, the tireless worker, with a thousand arrows, Rāvaṇa then struck Mātali with a flood of shafts.

sanskrit: pātayitvā rathopasthe rathāt ketuṃ ca kāñcanam aindrān abhijaghānāśvāñ śarajālena rāvaṇaḥ
english: Felling the golden banner from the chariot to its floor, Rāvaṇa also struck Indra's horses with a net of arrows.

sanskrit: viṣedur devagandharvā dānavāś cāraṇaiḥ saha rāmam ārtaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: Gods, gandharvas, and dānavas together with cāraṇas became despondent, and the siddhas and the great sages too, seeing Rāma distressed at that moment.

sanskrit: vyathitā vānarendrāś ca babhūvuḥ savibhīṣaṇāḥ rāmacandramasaṃ dṛṣṭvā grastaṃ rāvaṇarāhuṇā
english: The chiefs of the monkeys together with Vibhīṣaṇa also became troubled, seeing the moon of Rāma seized by the Rāhu of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: prājāpatyaṃ ca nakṣatraṃ rohiṇīṃ śaśinaḥ priyām samākramya budhas tasthau prajānām aśubhāvahaḥ
english: Mercury, boding ill for creatures, stood having occupied Rohiṇī, the moon's beloved constellation, which belongs to Prajāpati.

sanskrit: sadhūmaparivṛttormiḥ prajvalann iva sāgaraḥ utpapāta tadā kruddhaḥ spṛśann iva divākaram
english: The ocean, its waves encircled by smoke and blazing as if on fire, leaped up in fury as if touching the sun.

sanskrit: śastravarṇaḥ suparuṣo mandaraśmir divākaraḥ adṛśyata kabandhāṅgaḥ saṃsakto dhūmaketunā
english: The sun, its colour like a weapon, harsh and of dim radiance, appeared as if headless, conjoined with a comet.

sanskrit: kosalānāṃ ca nakṣatraṃ vyaktam indrāgnidaivatam ākramyāṅgārakas tasthau viśākhām api cāmbare
english: Mars stood clearly having occupied Viśākhā in the sky—the constellation presided over by Indra and Agni that belongs to the Kosalas.

sanskrit: daśāsyo viṃśatibhujaḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ adṛśyata daśagrīvo maināka iva parvataḥ
english: The ten-faced, twenty-armed one, holding his bow drawn, appeared—the ten-necked one visible like Mount Maināka.

sanskrit: nirasyamāno rāmas tu daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā nāśakad abhisaṃdhātuṃ sāyakān raṇamūrdhani
english: Rāma, being driven back by the ten-necked rākṣasa, was unable to fix his arrows in the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā bhrukuṭīṃ kruddhaḥ kiṃ cit saṃraktalocanaḥ jagāma sumahākrodhaṃ nirdahann iva cakṣuṣā
english: Then he, furrowing his brow in anger, his eyes slightly suffused with red, was seized with supreme wrath, as if scorching all things with his gaze.
